comments.textRawHtml:
2 anecdotes about Logitech software:

I had a high-end webcam that flickered. There should be switch in the software to switch from 50hz to 60hz that'd fix it but it was nowhere to be found. After digging deeper I found that it was only available in English version of software. It was before macOS had Setting to set language per app, so I had to manually replace Polish bundle with English one through binary.

Another one: Has K810 keyboard that started in "FN-by-default" mode. K811, Mac version of said keyboard allowed for changing default setting just as K810 on Windows, but K810 on Mac - no dice. Support told me to shell out 200€ on Mac keyboard so I ended up writing small binary switcher [0] that would run after keyboard got connected [0].

[0]: https://github.com/exlee/k810_fkeys_mac
comments.textZhHtml:
关于罗技软件的 2 个轶事：

我有一个闪烁的高端网络摄像头。软件中应该有从 50hz 切换到 60hz 的开关来解决这个问题，但无处可寻。经过深入研究，我发现它仅适用于英文版软件。当时 macOS 还没有为每个应用程序设置语言的设置，所以我必须通过二进制手动将波兰语捆绑包替换为英语捆绑包。

另一个：具有以“默认 FN”模式启动的 K810 键盘。 K811，Mac 版本的键盘允许更改默认设置，就像 Windows 上的 K810 一样，但 Mac 上的 K810 - 没有骰子。支持人员告诉我在 Mac 键盘上花 200 欧元，所以我最终编写了一个小型二进制切换器 [0]，它将在键盘连接后运行 [0]。

[0]: https://github.com/exlee/k810_fkeys_mac

> I had a high-end webcam that flickered. There should be switch in the software to switch from 50hz to 60hz that'd fix it but it was nowhere to be found.

Similar issue, although I'm not sure if it's the Logitech webcam or just how webcams are automatically configured on Linux these days in general: if I use a really bright LED lamp, the automatic exposure time goes down to the point that it doesn't matter if the webcam is set to 50hz or 60hz, it's going to catch flickering from other subtle frequencies affecting light output. I've also had situations where I wanted to use it to film a white piece of paper that I'm writing on, but it automatically adjusts exposure to make it gray instead.

It took me forever to find something with a straightforward GUI that lets me manually override this behavior on Linux. I ended up settling for cameractrls.

https://github.com/soyersoyer/cameractrls

children.author: xlii
children.textRawHtml:
I know that's a skill that I have, and I used it so many times it became effortless, but it all goes to one of jokes I like - that asks how do you eat an elephant. Easy - with a fork.

So in that particular case I have a keyboard and it's misbehaving. I know that by some dark magic I can make it behave as I want and that software on Windows can do that.

So I think, "ok, how does it communicate?" - with Bluetooth, obviously. So my next thought it: can I transmit over bluetooth magic bytes that do exactly like this. I definitely have a device on my computer, so I can try to make it.

From that it's all about "how to send arbitrary stuff from bluetooth" search. Instinct tells me there has to be a library, or that at least on person on world wide web tried to do something similar.

If I find even single instance of this, I'm home - read what they did, try to figure out if I can adjust it and do so. Hocus pocus - binary switcher happens.

Though, in the end, it's all about approach. I found many people say "I don't know how to do it, so I don't". My approach is "I rarely know what do, but that doesn't stop me from trying". And this trying new stuff brings practice for the next unknown endeavor.
children.textZhHtml:
我知道这是我拥有的一项技能，而且我使用了很多次，它变得毫不费力，但这一切都源于我喜欢的一个笑话 - 那问你如何吃掉大象。简单 - 用叉子。

所以在这种特殊情况下，我有一个键盘，但它表现不佳。我知道通过某种黑魔法我可以让它按照我想要的方式运行，Windows 上的软件也可以做到这一点。

所以我想，“好吧，它是如何通信的？” - 显然是通过蓝牙。所以我的下一个想法是：我可以通过蓝牙魔法字节进行传输吗？我的计算机上肯定有一个设备，所以我可以尝试制作它。

从这一切都是关于“如何从蓝牙发送任意内容”搜索。直觉告诉我必须有一个图书馆，或者至少在万维网上有人试图做类似的事情。

如果我发现哪怕是一个这样的例子，我就回家了 - 阅读他们做了什么，尝试弄清楚我是否可以调整它并这样做。 Hocus pocus - 二进制切换器发生了。

不过，最终，这都是关于方法的。我发现很多人说“我不知道该怎么做，所以我不做”。我的方法是“我很少知道该做什么，但这并不妨碍我尝试”。这种尝试新事物为下一个未知的尝试带来了练习。

Maybe the real issue is selective outrage about legal injustice. I totally agree that this was wrong and he should not have been prosecuted but a large part of the effort that dealt this injustice to him was facilitated by the fact that the vast majority of people willfully turn a blind eye when the same thing or worse happens to people are not of their ilk. If we were to finally stand up and say that justice for all means justice for ALL; we might be able to prevent the next Aaron Swartz.

They use this "scare tatic" so much and I understand why it works; the possibility of facing those years is terrifying. “也许真正的问题是对法律不公正的选择性愤怒。”

children.author: AnthonyMouse
children.textRawHtml:
> If it applied equally to everyone, then more people would be outraged as it affected them.

In order to do this you need to have laws that are designed to be reasonable for people to actually follow instead of laws that are designed to allow prosecutors to find a violation whenever they want to.

Actually enforcing them would create pressure to do that, but it would also create pressure to go back to selective enforcement when powerful people object to being subjected to the unreasonableness of existing laws.

A better solution might be to make a showing of selective enforcement a means to strike down a law. If you can show that someone else was doing the same thing without being charged then the prosecution either has to charge them too or that law is struck down and no one can be charged with it anymore.

Then instead of the incentive not to charge powerful people creating pressure for selective enforcement, the same incentive creates pressure to strike down the laws that can't reasonably be uniformly enforced.
children.textZhHtml:
> 如果它平等地适用于每个人，那么更多的人会因为它影响到他们而感到愤怒。

为了做到这一点，你需要制定合理的法律，让人们真正遵守，而不是旨在允许检察官随时发现违规行为的法律。

实际上执行这些法律会产生这样做的压力，但当有权势的人反对受到约束时，也会产生返回选择性执法的压力。现有法律的不合理性。

更好的解决方案可能是将选择性执法的表现作为废除法律的手段。如果你能证明其他人在没有受到指控的情况下做了同样的事情，那么检方要么必须对他们也提出指控，要么法律被废除，没有人可以再被指控。

然后，不是激励不起诉有权势的人，为选择性执法创造压力，同样的激励会产生压力，废除那些无法合理统一执行的法律。

> Model router is also a natural home for llm security - OpenRouter has the beginnings of prompt injection detection

Maybe I'm biased from the perspective of a "harness provider", but I think Model routers often have too little context to act as well-informed prompt injection prevention. e.g. it lacks context of where which part of the message(s) originates from and sanitization/safeguards were already performed on the application layer.

Something like OpenRouter's "flag" mode is fine, but usage of auto-redact or auto-block should really only be used if there is significant risk exposure through your harness or otherwise they are a constant source of bugs.

comments.author: afc
comments.textRawHtml:
> Both incidents were capacity failures at their core. We failed to scale critical components before demand exceeded their capacity.

This is the wrong way to think about this because there's no such thing as infinite capacity. A large distributed system will be simultaneously mostly idle and (in some subcomponents) overloaded. The root cause is not "a component didn't have enough capacity (because of auto scaling failures)", but rather "this complex system collapses (rather than degrade gracefully) when demand exceeds capacity".

When components reach capacity limits, the excess traffic of the lowest priority should be rejected. Rejected traffic should not be retried — in fact, not only should clients not retry these errors, these errors should cause client-side throttling. Traffic isolation should be applied — if the cause of the overload is a single client/customer system, no other system should be affected.

Nearly a decade ago I wrote about some of the techniques we applied at Google to implement these protections: https://sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload/ Most other large internet services have since copied them, afaik.
comments.textZhHtml:
> 这两起事件的核心都是容量故障。我们未能在需求超出其容量之前扩展关键组件。

这是错误的思考方式，因为不存在无限容量这样的事情。大型分布式系统将同时大部分处于空闲状态和（在某些子组件中）过载。根本原因不是“某个组件没有足够的容量（因为自动伸缩失败）”，而是“当需求超过容量时，这个复杂的系统就会崩溃（而不是优雅地降级）”。

当组件达到容量限制时，最低优先级的多余流量应该被拒绝。被拒绝的流量不应该重试——事实上，客户端不仅不应该重试这些错误，这些错误还应该导致客户端限制。应应用流量隔离 - 如果过载的原因是单个客户端/客户系统，则不应影响其他系统。

大约十年前，我写了一篇有关我们在 Google 为实现这些保护而应用的一些技术的文章：https://sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload/据我所知，大多数其他大型互联网服务都已复制它们。

> you want to move these decisions into the application tier as much as possible

I actually agree, but this is a luxury that most large companies cannot politically prioritize (it is not Product/Sales-driven, see earlier comment). Especially when the company is large, and there are dozens if not hundreds of developer teams in a polyglot microservice environment, pushing application-level handling of these concerns is virtually impossible without executive support, and because it doesn't move the bottom line in an easily measurable way, you won't get executive support.

Companies much prefer infrastructure-based solutions to these problems, even if they're coarser, because the relatively small number of people who need to be involved makes it politically feasible. Easy example off the top of my head - mutual TLS encrypting east-west traffic has been implementable at the application layer for decades, but it was a pipe dream until service meshes made it easy to deploy (it's still a pipe dream for many orgs that refuse to schedule any infra work not Product/Sales-driven though).

children.author: michaelt
children.textRawHtml:
> I'm assuming "playing silent audio" is a sufficiently common thing for websites to do to have motivated browsers into doing the slightly more complicated thing of actually analyzing audio streams for content

When most sites do browser fingerprinting using audio, they use an 'OfflineAudioContext' - which unlike a normal AudioContext, doesn't run in real time and send its output to system's loudspeakers; instead, it runs faster-than-real-time and outputs to an AudioBuffer. So the browser can easily tell no sound is being played.

For example - you can tell the browser to create a 10kHz square wave, feed it to a GainNode then a DynamicsCompressorNode, output to a buffer, then hash the contents of that buffer - which gives you a browser fingerprint, because of subtle differences between browsers.
children.textZhHtml:
> 我假设“播放无声音频”对于网站来说是很常见的事情，从而促使浏览器做稍微复杂一点的事情，即实际分析内容的音频流

当大多数网站使用音频进行浏览器指纹识别时，他们使用“OfflineAudioContext” - 与普通的 AudioContext 不同，它不会实时运行并将其输出发送到系统的扬声器；相反，它的运行速度比实时速度更快并输出到 AudioBuffer。因此，浏览器可以轻松判断没有播放任何声音。

例如 - 您可以告诉浏览器创建 10kHz 方波，将其馈送到 GainNode，然后馈送到 DynamicsCompressorNode，输出到缓冲区，然后散列该缓冲区的内容 - 由于浏览器之间存在细微差别，这会为您提供浏览器指纹。

stories.title: Google has stopped pushing Git tags for some Android source code

comments.author: grapheneos
comments.textRawHtml:
They stopped pushing tags for any of the Pixel kernel or userspace driver repositories to AOSP. They also stopped pushing AOSP releases specific to Pixels which is why AOSP now only gets yearly releases, QPR2 releases and security backports to both of those. Other OEMs use the yearly and theoretically also the QPR2 releases. Both the yearly and QPR2 releases get monthly security backports. Since they dropped Pixel support from AOSP, they don't push the releases not shipped by other OEMs anymore.

These changes directly led to our Motorola partnership. One of their security people reached out to us after seeing our posts about this with the launch of Android 16. We haven't talked about it much since then since we adapted to it during the several weeks it delayed our Android 16 port. We then continued adapting to it and have fully worked around it. It was an ongoing problem but not a new one and we had accepted we had to deal with it as the new normal.

They were previously responding to our kernel source requests within a day. It was often done without hours. Despite the archaic system, this part wasn't that bad. Recently, they've been taking weeks or longer to get back to us for the requests which is ridiculous. It's the direct result of purposely adding a lot of friction with manual handling of the requests even if the delays weren't directly planned by management.

Weeks or months of delay is not reasonable for one of the largest tech companies in the world. GPL doesn't set a standard time limit for providing the sources, but that doesn't mean they can delay it indefinitely. They need to do it in a reasonable amount of time. What's reasonable for one of the largest tech companies in the world in 2026 with current technology is not the same as what was reasonable 30 years ago. Google chose to come up with a archaic way of distributing the sources involving someone manually going through a list and sharing Google Drive access. It's a deliberate way of making it painful. If they can't keep up with it and it gets delayed for weeks or months then they're not complying with the GPL by not providing it in a reasonable amount of time. Law is not code and a time limit not being explicitly written down doesn't mean there isn't a limit to what's reasonable for compliance.

They'll sell far fewer Pixels because of these overall changes. It pushes GrapheneOS and other projects towards other devices instead. For us, Pixels are being used due to security rather than ease of supporting them. It's now a lot harder to deal with Pixels than it would be for many other devices but they're currently still the most secure option. We're working on changing that and have a lot less reason to contribute to improving Pixels. We helped them fix serious security weaknesses for Pixels including vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild by forensic data extraction companies. Pixel security with the stock OS would be worse without GrapheneOS.
comments.textZhHtml:
他们停止将任何 Pixel 内核或用户空间驱动程序存储库的标签推送到 AOSP。他们还停止推送特定于 Pixel 的 AOSP 版本，这就是为什么 AOSP 现在只获得年度版本、QPR2 版本以及这两个版本的安全向后移植。其他 OEM 厂商也使用每年发布的 QPR2 版本，理论上也是如此。年度版本和 QPR2 版本均获得每月安全向后移植。由于他们放弃了 AOSP 对 Pixel 的支持，因此他们不再推送其他 OEM 厂商未发布的版本。

这些变化直接促成了我们与摩托罗拉的合作关系。他们的一位安全人员在看到我们关于 Android 16 发布的帖子后联系了我们。从那以后我们就没有过多谈论它，因为我们在 Android 16 端口延迟的几周内适应了它。然后我们继续适应它并完全解决它。这是一个持续存在的问题，但不是一个新问题，我们已经接受必须将其作为新常态来处理。

他们之前在一天内响应了我们的内核源请求。这通常不需要几个小时就能完成。尽管系统陈旧，但这部分还不错。最近，他们花了几周或更长时间才回复我们的请求，这很荒谬。这是故意在手动处理请求时增加大量摩擦的直接结果，即使延迟不是由管理层直接计划的。

对于世界上最大的科技公司之一来说，数周或数月的延迟是不合理的。 GPL 没有设定提供源代码的标准时间限制，但这并不意味着他们可以无限期地推迟。他们需要在合理的时间内完成它。对于 2026 年世界上最大的科技公司之一来说，以现有技术来看，合理的做法与 30 年前的合理做法不同。谷歌选择提出一种古老的方式来分发源，需要有人手动浏览列表并共享谷歌云端硬盘访问权限。这是一种故意让它变得痛苦的方式。如果他们跟不上它并且延迟了几周或几个月，那么他们没有在合理的时间内提供它，就没有遵守 GPL。法律不是代码，没有明确写下的时间限制并不意味着对合理合规性没有限制。

由于这些总体变化，他们销售的像素会少得多。它将 GrapheneOS 和其他项目推向其他设备。对我们来说，使用 Pixel 是因为安全性而不是易于支持。现在处理 Pixel 比处理许多其他设备要困难得多，但它们仍然是目前最安全的选择。我们正在努力改变这一点，并且没有太多理由为提高像素做出贡献。我们帮助他们修复了 Pixel 的严重安全漏洞，包括被法医数据提取公司在野外利用的漏洞。如果没有 GrapheneOS，现有操作系统的像素安全性会更差。

comments.author: hibikir
comments.textRawHtml:
The anecdote about the garden of earthly delights is going to be relatable even for art students. I've met art teachers that ended up "trapped" in Madrid by the Prado Museum: A green, American future Ph.D student that was heading to Greece to specialize in old greek art. But instead of flying straight there, they stopped at Madrid to see the Prado, and were never able to leave. Changed their direction immediately, and ended up teaching in Madrid, and retiring there, because one of the countless masterpieces in there stole their life plans away.

There's more famous museums, and it doesn't have the most popular paintings for non specialist, but it's just haymaker after haymaker, in every single room. And that's leaving the modern art to the Reina Sofia, a short walk away. (Although I guess keeping late Goya there is kind of cheating, as I'd argue he becomes a pioneer of modern art after the war starts)

Books might require quite a bit of work before you can tell they are eternal masterpieces. Seeing the depths of some forms of music might involve not-so-impressive efforts earlier, just to get to the good parts. The very best paintings in the world, in person, can stop people cold. Large format efforts that demand attention even when you don't consider every single small decision.

The Garden of Earthly Delights used to be stuck in a corner, at the edge of one of the wings of the Prado. As if "oh well, I guess it fits here, near all the medieval art". It counted as an ambush.
comments.textZhHtml:
即使对于艺术系的学生来说，关于尘世欢乐花园的轶事也会产生共鸣。我遇到过一些艺术老师，他们最终被普拉多博物馆“困”在马德里：一位年轻的美国未来博士生，正前往希腊专门研究古希腊艺术。但他们没有直接飞到那里，而是在马德里停留参观普拉多，然后就再也无法离开。他们立即改变了方向，最终在马德里教书，并在那里退休，因为那里无数的杰作之一夺走了他们的人生计划。

这里有更多著名的博物馆，而且没有非专业人士最受欢迎的画作，但每个房间里都有一个又一个的干草人。 现在，现代艺术就交给了距离酒店仅几步之遥的索非亚王后国家艺术中心 (Reina Sofia)。 （虽然我猜戈雅迟到有点作弊，因为我认为他在战争开始后成为现代艺术的先驱）

书籍可能需要大量的工作才能让你知道它们是永恒的杰作。要了解某些形式的音乐的深度，可能需要付出不那么令人印象深刻的努力，只是为了到达好的部分。世界上最好的画作，亲眼所见，可以让人不再感到寒冷。即使您不考虑每一个小决定，大型作品也需要引起注意。

人间乐园曾经被困在普拉多一侧机翼边缘的一个角落里。 就好像“哦，好吧，我想它适合这里，靠近所有中世纪艺术”。这也算是一次伏击吧。

children.author: jameshart
children.textRawHtml:
Totally. The right way to approach an art gallery is definitely just to walk round until something hits you.

Most astonishing time that happened to me was a wall-sized Rothko that just floored me, in a way I never would have expected a slab of color to.

Dali’s La Gare de Perpignan stopped me in my tracks too.

Rarely been as stunned by more famous works as when I got blindsided by something that leapt out and said ‘look’.
children.textZhHtml:
完全。进入美术馆的正确方式绝对是四处走走，直到有什么东西 点击数 你。

发生在我身上最令人惊讶的一次是一幅墙壁大小的罗斯科作品让我摔倒在地，这是我从未想到过的一块颜色。

大理的 佩皮尼昂站 我也停下了脚步。

很少有比我被突然跳出来说“看”的东西让我措手不及的著名作品更令我震惊的了。

children.author: encomiast
children.textRawHtml:
Possibly the best thing about Washington D.C. is that the National Gallery of Art (along with, I think, all the Smithsonian) is free. This means you just take a casual stroll through without any of the pressure of having spent a sizable sum like you might to visit a place like the Art Institute in Chicago. In Chicago a visit is an event, you need to see the Seurat, the Grant Wood, etc. You've spent money and you need make it count.

In D.C. you can literally walk in, go look at the big Joan Mitchell for 10 minutes and continue on your day. Or you can wander through a room you've never been interested in and find something and then go to lunch. Without the commitment to get everything done, you are suddenly free.

Good libraries (edit: even mediocre libraries) also have this quality.
children.textZhHtml:
华盛顿特区最好的事情可能是国家美术馆（我认为还有所有史密森尼博物馆）都是免费的。这意味着您只需随意漫步，而无需像参观芝加哥艺术学院这样的地方那样花费大量金钱。在芝加哥，参观是一件大事，你需要参观修拉、格兰特伍德等。你花了钱，你需要让它发挥作用。

在华盛顿特区，您实际上可以走进去，花 10 分钟看看伟大的琼·米切尔 (Joan Mitchell)，然后继续您的一天。或者你可以在一个你从来不感兴趣的房间里闲逛，找到一些东西，然后去吃午饭。没有完成所有事情的承诺，你突然就自由了。

好的图书馆（编辑：即使是平庸的图书馆）也具有这种品质。

children.author: bluGill
children.textRawHtml:
Many museums have a membership. For one price you can visit the museum any time you want. I strongly recommend everyone do this for all their local museums. It changes the experience when you don't feel bad about wasting the admission because you only have an hour. Particularly small local museums where spending all day isn't worth it, but if you have to pay admission you feel compelled to spend all day to get your money's worth.

Some of them also include reduced price admission to others of the same time. My local zoo isn't very big, but the membership means half price admission to a very good zoo just a couple hours away. My local science museum got me free admission to many other science museums and children's museums. My local historic farm got me into a lot of interesting historical sites. Be sure to understand what you get and take advantage of it on vacations.

I strongly recommend you get the version that lets you bring two guests. When my parents or some other friend from out of town comes to visit we have something interesting to show them (and if they are not having fun we can leave early).
children.textZhHtml:
许多博物馆都有会员资格。只需支付一笔费用，您就可以随时参观博物馆。我强烈建议每个人为他们当地的所有博物馆都这样做。 当你不因为只有一个小时而浪费门票而感到难过时，它会改变体验。特别小的当地博物馆，在那里花一整天是不值得的，但如果你必须支付入场费，你会觉得不得不花一整天才能让你的钱花得值。

其中一些博物馆还包括向其他同一时间的其他博物馆提供折扣门票。 我当地的动物园不是很大，但是会员资格意味着可以半价进入一个非常好的动物园，距离酒店只有几个小时的路程。我当地的科学博物馆让我可以免费参观许多其他科学博物馆和儿童博物馆。我当地历史悠久的农场让我参观了许多有趣的历史遗迹。请务必了解您将获得什么并在假期中充分利用它。

我强烈建议您购买可携带两位客人的版本。当我的父母或其他外地朋友来看望我们时，我们会向他们展示一些有趣的东西（如果他们不开心，我们可以提前离开）。

children.author: azath92
children.textRawHtml:
For those of us on the other side of the ditch: all museums in London are free. and I would echo the sentiment that it makes exploration of them less of a completionist activity to "get your monies worth" and more of an enjoyable forey into a rich space.

Its literally a paradigm shift.

Also almost all commercial art galleries are like this, obvs for other reasons. The gallery district (google art galleries then wander those streets, chelsea is the most established) in NYC is an amazing place to spend a day wandering around seeing amazing art. my uncle who teaches art introduced me to it and i try to spread the word.

Free art for any reason is amazing.
children.textZhHtml:
对于我们这些在沟渠另一边的人来说：伦敦的所有博物馆都是免费的。我同意这样的观点，即它使得对它们的探索不再是“让你的钱物有所值”的完成主义活动，而是更多地进入一个丰富的空间，这是一种令人愉快的尝试。

这实际上是一种范式转变。

此外，几乎所有商业艺术画廊都是这样的，出于其他原因。纽约的画廊区（谷歌艺术画廊然后在这些街道上漫步，切尔西是最古老的）是一个令人惊叹的地方，可以花一天的时间漫步欣赏令人惊叹的艺术。我教艺术的叔叔向我介绍了它，我尝试传播这个词。

任何原因的免费艺术都是令人惊叹的。

But let’s not pretend that the plastic and painterly arts are so much more self-evidently “thick” than literature is. Despite their immediacy, these arts have their own conventions, motifs, and demands that must be understood to “find the treasure in the dark cave.”

I have tried to convince someone I know that an art museum merits more than a one-minute-per-painting, four minutes-max-per-room, pretty/not-pretty approach. She still does not understand why I linger over books or works of art, and I have not the wherewithal to lead her through the techniques, the conventions, or the history that makes this worthwhile for me.
children.textZhHtml:
但我们不要假装造型艺术和绘画艺术比文学更不言而喻的“厚重”。尽管这些艺术具有即时性，但它们有自己的惯例、主题和要求，必须理解这些惯例、主题和要求，才能“在黑暗的洞穴中找到宝藏”。

我试图说服我认识的人，艺术博物馆的价值不仅仅是每幅画一分钟、每个房间最多四分钟、漂亮/不漂亮的方法。她仍然不明白为什么我对书籍或艺术作品流连忘返，而且我没有足够的资金来引导她了解使这对我来说有价值的技术、惯例或历史。

children.author: dredmorbius
children.textRawHtml:
There's a very widespread confusion over the meaning of inalienable.

The word does not mean "cannot be refused". It is trivially possible to refuse someone the right to life (kill them), liberty (imprison them), or happiness (torture them).

What cannot be done, however, is to transfer those rights to another individual.

Chattel or real property rights by contrast are inherently alienable. Your property (objects, land) can be denied you and given to someone else.

That said, the argument that inalienability makes a right somehow privileged (I have an an inalienable right to pain, for example, which I might be quite happy to shed) is a curious one, and there's a longer discussion in philosophy and the rights discourse over just what constitutes fundamental rights and why.

Definitions: "That cannot be transferred to another or others. Incapable of being alienated or transferred to another; that cannot or should not be transferred or given up."

<https://www.wordnik.com/words/inalienable>
children.textZhHtml:
对于inalienable的含义存在非常普遍的混淆。

这个词not的意思是“不能被拒绝”。 拒绝某人的生命权（杀死他们）、自由权（监禁他们）或幸福权（折磨他们）是微不足道的。

但是，不能将这些权利转让给另一个人。

动产权或不动产权利相比之下，本质上是可转让的。 你的财产（物体、土地）可能会被剥夺并交给别人。

也就是说，“不可剥夺性”使得一项权利在某种程度上享有特权（例如，我有一种不可剥夺的痛苦权利，我可能很乐意放弃它），这是一个奇怪的观点，并且在哲学和权利话语中对什么构成基本权利进行了更长的讨论和为什么。

定义：“不能转让给另一个人或其他人。不能被转让或转让给另一个人；不能或不应该转让或放弃。”

<https://www.wordnik.com/words/inalienable>

comments.author: dajonker
comments.textRawHtml:
Popover, dialog, invoker commands, our entire production app uses these everywhere and it works really well! The fact that dialogs and popovers are rendered on the "top layer" and that nested popovers are also automatically stacked on top of each other and have 'cascading close' shows how well these standards were designed.

The only hard thing is still to position a popover near the element that triggers it, such as when you want to create a context menu that has to render above/below the button that triggered it. There is anchor positioning in CSS now but support is still limited and I find it hard to wrap my head around.

LLMs are also terrible at these new standards. If they even know about them, they often think they're not baseline yet and they have almost zero training data compared to the giant mountain of weird JS and CSS that people had to use before the introduction of these standards.

top: anchor(bottom);

I'm not sure how widely supported it is but I've been using it in Firefox/Chrome.
